title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 53-54
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 53 to 54 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'उत्तरो गोपतिर्गोप्ता ज्ञानगम्यः पुरातनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 53 to 54 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 53 to 54.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 53 to 54** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **उत्तरो गोपतिर्गोप्ता ज्ञानगम्यः पुरातनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**उत्तरो गोपतिर्गोप्ता ज्ञानगम्यः पुरातनः । शरीरभूतभृद्भोक्ता कपीन्द्रो भूरिदक्षिणः ॥** **सोमपोऽमृतपः सोमः पुरुजित्पुरुसत्तमः । विनयो जयः सत्यसन्धो दाशार्हः सात्वतां पतिः ॥**

He is higher than all, the lord and guardian of cows. The one reached through knowledge, the ancient one, is that God of gods. He carries every embodied being, he is the enjoyer, lord of the monkeys and giver of great gifts. He drinks the soma and the nectar and shines as the Moon. The conqueror of many, the best of beings, is that God of gods. Humility, victory, true to his word, the lord of the Dasharhas and the Satvatas.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 53 to 54 mean?
faq.a: He is higher than all, the lord and guardian of cows. The one reached through knowledge, the ancient one, is that God of gods. He carries every embodied being, he is the enjoyer, lord of the monkeys and giver of great gifts. He drinks the soma and the nectar and shines as the Moon. The conqueror of many, the best of beings, is that God of gods. Humility, victory, true to his word, the lord of the Dasharhas and the Satvatas.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
